messages:
zoe: morning team — first week and blocked on k8s access. `kubectl get pods -n data-pipelines` returns Forbidden. kubeconfig shows a dev context but not sure why.

infra-jamie: welcome! :wave: quick checks: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n data-pipelines` please.

zoe: current-context=redwood-dev-zoe. `kubectl auth can-i` -> no.

mike: usually means RBAC or missing group mapping. Did you fill the infra access form at https://redwood.corp/onboard/infra-access and select the namespaces?

zoe: i only completed HR onboarding. will submit the infra form now. also my kubeconfig uses an SSO exec plugin — is that ok?

infra-jamie: exec auth is expected. After you submit, our bot applies the RoleBinding for group:eng-newhires to the namespaces you requested. It can take ~10 minutes.

zoe: submitted for namespace=data-pipelines.

sre-bot: access-request queued for user=zoe namespaces=[data-pipelines] (req=ar-91233). Processing...

mike: while you wait, avoid sharing raw kubeconfigs. To debug, run `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` and paste only `kubectl auth can-i` output or `kubectl config current-context`. If you must share a config, remove exec tokens first.

infra-jamie: access applied (req=ar-91233) -> RoleBinding added in data-pipelines for group:eng-newhires role=view.

zoe: re-checking: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n data-pipelines` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n data-pipelines` shows several pods. thanks!

mike: welcome aboard and FYI we recommend creating a per-repo kubeconfig (`kubectl config view --minify --flatten > .kubeconfig`) and using `export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/.kubeconfig:$HOME/.kube/config` to avoid accidental prod access.

zoe: saved — appreciate the help :tada:
